text:
Eli: throwing out an idea: instead of approving bundles by hand in the UI, what if the operator imports a short-lived activation-token file (on USB) that carries a hash-locked approval for a specific activation-group?
Nora: curious, so token is like a capability that nodes can check without contacting the proxy? how does that affect chain-of-custody?
Eli: it's a sealed token: token = Sign_Kop( group_id || expiry || nonce || hashlocker ) where hashlocker = H(secret), and operator reveals secret when doing the local challenge. token itself is logged and signed by the proxy too.
Jun: walk me through sequence: operator plugs USB -> imports token -> node sidecar sees token and activates? need to avoid single-person approval risk.
Eli: two-person flow: operator A imports token (creates a draft), operator B executes reveal step on console which unlocks token by providing preimage to the proxy. proxy records operator identities and signs the unlock event. nodes accept activation only when they see an unlocked token signed by proxy and signed approval record is present locally.
Leah: benefit is offline activation without always-on proxy. nodes verify signatures + that unlock timestamp <= token.expiry. Good for remote sites.
Nora: threat model: physical attacker could drop malicious token on USB. How do we ensure token was created by HQ and not adversary?
Eli: tokens must be generated by HQ signing key (private offsite). For higher security, require HSM where signing keys never leave HQ. proxy still verifies signature chain.
Jun: operational note: tokens must be short lived (hours) and single-use. we should include revocation list capability for when a token is lost.
Leah: revocation offline is tricky. maybe tokens include a revocation-hash tree root published in a later bundle; nodes only accept tokens if they match allowed roots. That pushes revocation to next sync window.
security-bot: reminder: include requirement for operator 2FA and audit log in RFC.
Eli: config sketch:
```yaml
activation_token:
  allowed_signers: ["/etc/keys/hq-root.pub"]
  max_ttl: 6h
  require_two_person: true
  revocation_policy: sync-on-next-bundle # options: immediate-online|sync-on-next-bundle
  single_use: true
```
Nora: what about canary/partial rollouts? tokens could be scoped to node selectors (labels) so you can unlock for a subset.
Jun: nodes need to be able to validate token without full blob download. token should include content digests and node will verify local artifact digests before activation.
Leah: implement streaming-verify API on sidecar: `verify-artifact --digest sha256:... --range` that checks piecewise without whole copy.
Eli: runbook snippet: if operator loses token USB -> treat as compromise: add token id to revocation list and perform emergency rollback; ops-bot will trigger cluster lockdown.
ops-bot: FYI: automation: `catalogctl import-token /mnt/usb/token.json` will return draft-id and a short qr code for second operator to scan for reveal step.
Nora: UX question: do we surface token details in console? operators want to see artifact list and size before revealing. exposing full artifact list in draft view seems fine.
Jun: dev concern: how do we avoid making nodes accept stale unlocked tokens replayed later? include monotonic nonce and expiry and require nodes to store seen nonces for single-use tokens. GC that store with TTL > max_ttl.
Leah: GC note: nodes store small seen-token index (sha256 nonces) with local LRU and TTL. central proxy mirrors seen nonces in audits when online.
Eli: open decision: revocation policy default. proposal: sync-on-next-bundle by default (works offline), but allow immediate-online for connected sites.
Nora: next steps: short RFC that specifies token format, signature chain, unlock protocol, and threat scenarios + proofs. Jun and Leah volunteer for PoC sidecar changes.
Jun: i'll prototype token validation and single-use nonce store.
Leah: i'll do the console/cli draft for import + reveal UX.
Eli: i'll draft RFC and include sample token JSON and sequence diagram. target: RFC by EOD Wednesday.
